headline: Bulog Intensifies Maize Procurement To Protect Local Farmer Income
metaDescription: The Ministry of Agriculture directs Bulog to proactively procure maize from farmers to ensure stable prices and prevent financial losses for producers.
aiSummaryBullets: Agriculture Minister Amran Sulaiman mandates that Bulog proactively purchase maize to protect farmers from price manipulation.
A minimum purchase price of Rp5,500 per kilogram is established as a floor, with businesses permitted to pay higher rates to farmers.
Bulog regional offices in East Nusa Tenggara, Jakarta, and Banten are actively scaling up maize absorption to stabilize the domestic market.
aiContextParagraph: The Indonesian government is currently focusing on stabilizing the national maize market by increasing state-led procurement efforts. Agriculture Minister Amran Sulaiman has instructed the state logistics agency, Bulog, to actively purchase maize from local producers to prevent price volatility and ensure that farmers do not suffer financial losses. As part of this policy, the government has set a floor price of Rp5,500 per kilogram, though it explicitly allows businesses to offer higher prices to farmers, viewing it as a mechanism for fair competition. These measures are being implemented alongside regional initiatives, with Bulog branches in East Nusa Tenggara, Jakarta, and Banten reporting active efforts to absorb local yields. The initiative follows broader government directives aimed at strengthening the national supply chain, which also seek to benefit poultry farmers by ensuring consistent and affordable feed availability across the country.
whyItIsViral: The topic is experiencing moderate momentum, with steady coverage from two major independent news outlets emphasizing government intervention in national food security.
